relevance_note: Case report of two males with Danon disease and LAMP2 variants plus a carrier family: "This study reports 2 male DD patients with distinct LAMP2 mutations".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (no tables in it); a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked that every span is verbatim. Scope: Case 1 (proband II-4, labelled "Case 1" because the paper uses that label most) and his family: mother I-2 and sisters II-1, II-2 (carriers of the same variant) and sister II-3 (tested, variant not detected; no variant row). Case 2 and his mother, father and sister (all tested, deletion not detected; no variant rows). No previously published individual gets a row: the Discussion mentions earlier variants (IVS6 + 5G > C, c.560-1G > A, intron 1 and 5 variants) only at the level of mutations, not persons. Choices: the relatives' sex comes from "sisters"; the sisters' inheritance is left 'not reported' although the mother carries the variant, because the paper states only the proband's segregation; relatives' variant type, zygosity and pathogenicity are 'not reported' (stated only for the proband). Case 1's "novel" mutation is not recorded as a pathogenicity class; ACMG guidelines were followed but no class or criteria are printed for either variant. Case 2's deletion has no cDNA or coordinates ("specific base pair coordinates unavailable"); variant type 'large deletion/CNV' is from "hemizygous loss spanning the entire exon 1". Case 2's family members are 'mother of Case 2' etc. Age at onset "in childhood" comes from the Discussion statement about both patients. Normal findings: whole-investigation normals (echocardiogram, ECG, myocardial enzymes, EMG) are recorded as written and do not exclude specific checklist items (D-27); the mother's "echocardiogram showed no abnormalities" therefore leaves LVH 'not reported'. The mother's AST 46 to 59 U/L is not recorded because no reference range is printed beside it. Case 1's "typically showed no symptoms of skeletal muscle impairment, such as weakness..." is recorded as excluded (note the hedge "typically"); the checklist item "proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)" is left 'not reported' for Case 1 because his biopsy shows vacuolar myopathic changes. "No abnormalities in motor development" and "no abnormalities ... in intelligence" are narrower than the composite checklist items, which stay 'not reported'. Lab values for Case 2 (INR, PT, ESR, NT-proBNP, urea, CK-MB) are recorded as observed only where the printed value lies outside the printed reference range. Contradictions: (1) Case 2 "showed signs of weakness from childhood" and exercise intolerance vs Discussion "neither shows obvious cognitive impairment or skeletal muscle lesion symptoms" (both rows emitted; checklist muscle item 'not reported'). (2) Abstract CK 3867 U/L (Case 1) and 5210 U/L (Case 2) vs text CK 1555 U/L and 482 U/L (may be different time points). (3) Abstract "died of heart failure 8 months after diagnosis" vs text admission January 2019 and death May 2020. (4) "the same mutation was also found in his mother, sisters (II-1, II-2), whose electrocardiogram and echocardiography were normal" could be read to include the mother, whose ECG showed atrial fibrillation; I applied "whose" to the sisters only. (5) Case 1 muscle LAMP2 immunohistochemistry is described as "only a few intracytoplasmic vacuoles" expressing LAMP2 in the Results and as "LAMP2 protein is positive" in the Discussion. (6) Case 1 echo measurements are introduced as "ECG revealed concentric left ventricular hypertrophy" (likely echocardiography).
